subject: general
question: In which layer of the atmosphere is ozone most concentrated?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Stratosphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stratosphere**

 
 
• The Stratosphere, the **second layer of the atmosphere**, contains the greatest concentration of ozone molecules **(approximately 90%)**.
 
• The **"ozone layer" **is the area in the stratosphere with the highest ozone content.
 
• The ozone layer, which is naturally present **6 to 30 miles above the Earth's surface, protects life on the planet from the damaging effects of ultraviolet radiation from the sun**.
 
• Three oxygen atoms are present in the molecule of ozone **(O₃)**.
 
• The natural quantity of ozone in the stratosphere is a result of a** balance between sunlight, which produces ozone, and chemical processes, which destroy it**.
 
• Ozone molecules are continuously generated and destroyed in the stratosphere.
 
• The **Troposphere, Stratosphere, Mesosphere, and Ionosphere **are the four atmospheric layers that make up the atmosphere.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Troposphere:**

 
 
• All of **Earth's weather occurs in the troposphere, which is the lowest part of the atmosphere**.
 
• The troposphere is **bounded on top by the tropopause**, a layer of air that separates the troposphere from the stratosphere, **and on the bottom it is bounded by the Earth's surface**.
 
 
 
• **Mesosphere:**
 
 
• The mesosphere lies** below the thermosphere and directly above the stratosphere.**
 
• It covers a distance of between** 31 and 53 miles **above our planet.** **
 
• The mesosphere's temperature drops with** altitude.**
 
 
 
• **Thermosphere:**
 
 
• It is located directly **above the mesosphere and below the exosphere**.
 
• The thermosphere makes up the majority of the ionosphere because ultraviolet energy inside this layer of the atmosphere promotes **photoionization/photodissociation** of molecules, creating ions.
